conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 1/19/23
conflicts.issue: Immediate Approval vs. One-Week Delay of Growing Together Elementary Assignment Rules
conflicts.summary: Board members broadly supported Growing Together's long-term equity goals but split over whether to adopt the elementary assignment rules immediately on January 19 ahead of the February 6 magnet application deadline or delay one week to publish written FAQs, regional maps, and school-specific answers for families and teachers.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the Growing Together elementary rules immediately so families and principals have definitive rules before the February 6 magnet window closes
side_a_arguments: Implementation does not take effect until 2024-25 (18 months away), and delaying one week would not change the underlying plan while shortening notice before the February 6 magnet lottery deadline.
Administrators and principals needed formal board authorization to publish concrete, address-specific communications, geocoded tools, and school-level outreach.
conflicts.side_b_position: Delay the vote until written FAQs and clear transition details for sunsetting magnets and staff are published to rebuild community trust
side_b_arguments: Board members and families—especially at Club Boulevard, R.N. Harris, Sandy Ridge, and Little River—still had unanswered questions about sunsetting magnets, fourth/fifth grade transfer rules, sibling rules, and teacher transfers.
Voting before publishing written FAQs risked deepening distrust and accelerating teacher and family departures.
conflicts.resolution: Natalie Beyer voiced support for a one-week delay during debate and requested a straw poll, then ultimately voted Aye alongside Umstead, Lewis, Valladares, Chávez, and Sears to pass the rules 6-1, with Millicent Rogers casting the sole Nay vote.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/17/22
conflicts.issue: Procedural Process vs. Immediate First-Reading Adoption of Draft LGBTQ+ Gender Support Policy
conflicts.summary: Board members debated whether to vote immediately on a member-drafted LGBTQ+ policy on first reading or follow formal agenda-notice procedures by directing staff and legal counsel to bring a vetted Orange County-model policy to the next meeting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance a foundational policy immediately rather than waiting for task force completion or further delay.
side_a_arguments: Community families have advocated for months and expect visible leadership to put a baseline policy in the policy manual.
Policies adapted from Orange and Buncombe counties are already vetted and reviewed by members and can be revised later as a living document.
Passing a formal directive ensures accountability rather than relying on informal expectations.
conflicts.side_b_position: Follow formal governance notice procedures and clarify whether administration is revising existing Gender Support Guidelines or drafting a new policy before voting.
side_b_arguments: The item was added to the agenda solely for discussion, not as a posted action item or first reading for public notice.
Passing policy without a finalized document posted on the agenda ahead of time departs from the board's governance and policy-committee process.
Board Attorney Rod Malone recommended directing staff and counsel to bring a reviewed draft to the next meeting, when the board could waive second reading if satisfied.
conflicts.resolution: The board reached consensus and voted 7-0 on Alexandra Valladares's motion (seconded by Natalie Beyer) directing administration to bring an LGBTQ+ gender support policy based on the Orange County model to the next board meeting, paired with a time-limited task force.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 9/22/22
conflicts.issue: City of Durham Request to Mount ShotSpotter Acoustic Sensors on DPS School Buildings
conflicts.summary: Board members debated a City of Durham request for an MOA allowing ShotSpotter gunshot detection devices to be mounted on school parapet walls, weighing intergovernmental deference and potential response-time benefits against student surveillance concerns.
conflicts.side_a_position: Decline mounting ShotSpotter surveillance devices on school buildings and focus city-school partnerships on root causes of gun violence.
side_a_arguments: Placing acoustic surveillance equipment on school buildings sends an undesirable message to students and represents excessive surveillance.
Other mounting locations exist for the city's already-approved project, making school buildings unnecessary.
Collaboration with the city should prioritize addressing the root causes of gun violence, and some expressed interest in a buffer zone around schools.
conflicts.side_b_position: Respect the City Council's approved ShotSpotter pilot and consider potential emergency response-time benefits.
side_b_arguments: Durham City Council already voted to approve ShotSpotter, and inter-body collaboration favors deferring to the city's judgment on its program.
Acoustic detection could provide single-digit-second improvements in emergency response time if shots are fired near a school.
conflicts.resolution: Board Attorney Rod Malone advised that a motion was only needed to move forward with an MOA, not to decline it. No board member made a motion to proceed, so the administration took no action to place ShotSpotter devices on DPS schools.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 1/26/23
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 26, 2023 monthly meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard extensive public comment from teachers opposing a February 1 fire-code enforcement deadline removing personal classroom refrigerators and microwaves, as well as student comments on exam exemptions and Gaggle monitoring. In response, the board unanimously approved emergency funding for 147 commercial refrigerators and 208 microwaves across schools (over $300,000 from lapsed salaries) and pushed the compliance deadline to April 1, 2023. The board also unanimously adopted a Safe Routes to School NCDOT grant resolution, received Strategic Plan Priority 3 (human resources/turnover at 19.8%), 10-year capital/2022 GO bond cost escalation ($70 million shortfall on design-phase projects), and FY23-24 budget previews ($10.8 million classified salary study ask), deferred the ESSER update to February, and approved the personnel report and an employee dismissal resolution after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order, paused briefly for YouTube technical issues, and joined communications staff in honoring December and January Students, Teachers, and Employees of the Month (including Ignite Online Academy, Northern High, Hillside High, and Mangum Elementary). Superintendent Pascal Mubenga then delivered his update.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Minutes, and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board amended the agenda to add the Safe Routes to School resolution and appliance budgetary items and approved the prior monthly minutes. During public comment, numerous educators—including Riley Finnegan and others—urged delaying the February 1 ban on personal classroom microwaves and refrigerators and warned of workload and lunch-break impacts, while student speakers urged revising exam exemption rules and questioned Gaggle privacy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Items and Safe Routes to School Grant Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After approving consent items (including Carrington Middle School chillers with Jeff Hargett Mechanical and the monthly change order report), Executive Director Matthew Palmer and Kristen Brookshire presented a resolution authorizing DPS to serve as lead applicant for a three-year (2023-2026) NCDOT Safe Routes to School non-infrastructure grant in partnership with Bike Durham and the City of Durham. Board members praised expanding biking and walking infrastructure across elementary, middle, and high schools.

agenda_items.title: School Appliance Budgetary Allocation and Fire-Code Compliance Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following meetings with the Fire Marshal, Superintendent Mubenga and CFO Paul LeSieur proposed allocating lapsed-salary funds (over $300,000, covering 147 refrigerators at $2,000 each and 208 microwaves at $350 each per school requests) directly to schools and extending the fire-code compliance deadline from February 1 to April 1, 2023. While Natalie Beyer questioned why dorms allowed appliances and criticized how the dispute played out in the press, board members unanimously approved the expenditure to protect both building safety and staff working conditions.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 3 Update: Attracting and Retaining Educators
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Arasi Bozarth/Dr. Alvera Lesane and HR leaders presented Priority 3 metrics showing 2021-22 and December 2022 teacher turnover at 19.8% (missing the 14.3% target), Hispanic/Latino staff representation at 6% (below 8%), and employee satisfaction at 86.8% (below 89%). Board members discussed job-sharing for retirees, stay interviews, school culture, bilingual educator pipelines, and international credentialing barriers, and voted unanimously to defer the ESSER funding update (including Gaggle) to the February work session.

agenda_items.title: 10-Year Capital Improvement Plan and 2022 GO Bond Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and Frederick Davis reviewed progress on the $423 million 2022 GO bond—including Murray-Massenburg groundbreaking, DSA's new Duke Homestead site design, and priority renovations—while warning that construction inflation (roughly 1% per month) left an estimated $70 million shortfall on already-designed projects. Board members discussed potentially prioritizing conversion of the old Northern High School for CTE after August 2023 and ensuring gender-neutral restrooms in new school designs.

agenda_items.title: FY 2023-24 Budget Development Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur outlined initial FY23-24 budget pressures, including projected 4.2% certified and 4% classified salary increases, rising retirement (25.75%) and health benefit costs ($4.9 million), a $10.8 million county request for the classified salary study ($9 million plus $1.8 million charter share), and the loss of 24 state teaching positions due to declining enrollment. Board members requested staffing support for Growing Together, timelines for the $18 million MacKenzie Scott plan, and planning for the 2024 ESSER cliff.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, Personnel Report, and Employee Dismissal Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session with an added real-property negotiation item under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5), and upon returning at 05:24:34 unanimously approved the January 26, 2023 personnel report and a separate resolution for the dismissal of an employee.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 1/19/23
meetings.executive_summary: At a four-hour special meeting on January 19, 2023 (presided over in person by Vice Chair Matt Sears while Chair Bettina Umstead and Board Member Jovonia Lewis joined virtually), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education voted 6-1 to adopt the Growing Together elementary school assignment rules under Policy 4150 and the secondary program timeline for implementation in 2024-25. Administration opened with revised compromises guaranteeing fourth- and fifth-grade legacy seats, regional continuity for Montessori, IB, and year-round students, and converting Little River to K-5 Montessori rather than K-8. More than 45 public speakers—including Little River teachers and Club Boulevard, Morehead, and Sandy Ridge parents—urged delaying the vote due to unanswered questions and transition anxiety, sparking extensive board debate before Natalie Beyer joined the majority to pass the rules 6-1 with Millicent Rogers dissenting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Matt Sears called the special meeting to order, confirmed virtual attendance by Chair Bettina Umstead and Board Member Jovonia Lewis, and conducted a 7-0 roll call vote to move the Growing Together administration presentation ahead of general public comment.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together Elementary Rules Update (Policy 4150)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy outlined updated Growing Together recommendations for 2024-25: fourth and fifth graders may remain at current schools, current DLI/Montessori/IB/year-round students will be guaranteed continued program seats within their region, all elementary schools will offer weekly world languages, arts, and STEM, and Little River will transition to K-5 Montessori starting with pre-K, kindergarten, and one lower-elementary class rather than K-8.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Action deferred until after public comment

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment on Growing Together
agenda_items.discussion_summary: More than 45 speakers addressed the board under two-minute limits, including Little River educators (such as Candice Diamond and Erica McCray) warning of staff turnover and inadequate communication, Club Boulevard and Sandy Ridge parents seeking clarity on sunsetting magnet programs, and multilingual families like Hortencia Garcia requesting stronger outreach and legacy protections.

agenda_items.title: Board Deliberation and Roll Call Vote on Growing Together Elementary Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jovonia Lewis moved (seconded by Alexandra Valladares) to approve the Growing Together elementary rules for Policy 4150 and secondary timeline, triggering over two hours of debate on bus route savings (188 down to 130 routes in full modeling versus ~50 added buses per legacy grade), seat-capacity math, sibling preference, and whether to delay one week for written FAQs. In the final roll call at 04:04:15, six members voted Aye and Millicent Rogers voted Nay.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 1/12/23
meetings.executive_summary: At its nearly seven-hour January 12, 2023 work session (with Alexandra Valladares attending virtually), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously adopted a National Mentoring Month resolution, approved the 2023 Legislative Agenda, and waived second reading to adopt amended LGBTQIA+ and Gender Support Policy 1735/435. The board received the HIL Consultants classified employee salary study recommending a 30-step schedule costing approximately $10.8 million to address pay compression for ~2,200 classified staff, plus a comprehensive DPS transportation overview covering Edulog parent app deployment and bus driver shortages. The evening concluded with over two and a half hours of contentious public comment and board questioning on the newly released Growing Together elementary assignment and legacy rules ahead of the January 19 special meeting vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and December 8, 2022 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the work session, noted Alexandra Valladares was attending virtually from Texas, and led voice votes approving the agenda and the December 8, 2022 work session minutes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dozens of Little River teachers and Montessori/magnet parents (including Carrie Cummings, Julie Applewhite, James Gutto, Jessica Hart, Travis Morrison, Nathan Wheeler, and Megan Hudson) urged the board to delay voting on the Growing Together elementary rules released on January 9, criticizing the two-year unpaid summer Montessori training requirement and requesting legacy protections for enrolled students.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda, National Mentoring Month Resolution, and 2023 Legislative Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the consent agenda, adopted a January 2023 National Mentoring Month proclamation presented by Jovonia Lewis in partnership with local mentoring nonprofits, and adopted the 2023 Legislative Agenda (prioritizing Leandro funding, compensation, flexible school safety funding, equity, universal school meals, and mental health).

agenda_items.title: Classified Employee Salary Study Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Alvera Lesane and HIL Consultants (Hank Hurd and Frank Lopes) presented the classified salary study impacting roughly 2,200 employees, detailing severe pay compression since 2008 and proposing a 30-step salary schedule estimated at $10.8 million, with an additional review of ~65 coordinator-and-above positions slated for April.

agenda_items.title: Amended LGBTQIA+ and Gender Support Policy (Policy 1735)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented revisions to the LGBTQIA+ and Gender Support policy adopted on first reading in December, including replacing 'preferred' with 'chosen' names and pronouns, removing 'allied' from the LGBTQIA+ acronym at Emily Chávez's request, adding curriculum selection language, and harmonizing policy terminology. Matt Sears moved—and amended his motion at Natalie Beyer's suggestion—to waive second reading and adopt the amended policy immediately.

agenda_items.title: DPS Transportation Overview of 2023 Initiatives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matthew Palmer, Director Joe Harris, and Assistant Director Annie Fullwood reviewed transportation operations, Edulog parent app rollout, and bus driver recruitment/retention efforts. Board members requested follow-up feedback from drivers and monitors on the Edulog app and asked HR to explore part-time partnerships with City of Durham transit drivers.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together Elementary Rules Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy, Melody Marshall, and the Growing Together team presented the 2024-25 elementary boundaries, five regional zones (with W.G. Pearson serving all regions), expanded application seats (17%-22% across regions), and proposed legacy and Montessori/DLI transition rules. Board members questioned separate-setting special education placements, fourth/fifth-grade legacy options, Little River's K-8 transition, and family outreach ahead of the January 19 vote.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After summarizing staff follow-up items, the board entered closed session by roll call vote at 06:17:26, returned at 06:53:20, unanimously approved the January 12, 2023 personnel report by roll call, and adjourned.

votes.discussion_detail: Proclaimed January 2023 as National Mentoring Month and added board member signature lines.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the six-point 2023 legislative agenda covering Leandro funding, staff compensation, flexible school safety funding, equity, universal school meals, and mental health.

meetings.title: Durham Delegates Meeting | January 5, 2023 | 9:00AM
meetings.executive_summary: On January 5, 2023, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education and senior administration hosted a morning legislative breakfast with members of Durham's North Carolina General Assembly delegation—including Senators Natalie Murdock and Mike Woodard and Representatives Marcia Morey, Zach Hawkins, and Ray Jeffers. Board members previewed their draft 2023 legislative agenda (scheduled for formal vote on January 12), emphasizing flexible state school safety funding not restricted to placing SROs in every school, teacher and Exceptional Children staff vacancies, retiree rehire restrictions, master's pay, universal school meals, and state capital bond needs for buildings averaging 45 years old. Legislators shared perspectives on urban supplement exclusions, upcoming K-3 parental rights legislation, truancy/homeschool tracking, and the need for DPS fact sheets to advocate with Republican education committee chairs.

agenda_items.title: Introductions and Draft 2023 DPS Legislative Agenda Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members of the Durham legislative delegation and DPS school board introduced themselves, after which Chair Bettina Umstead presented the board's draft 2023 legislative agenda focused on pandemic recovery and educator/student support. Board members highlighted opposition to restricting state school safety grants solely to placing police officers in every school, arguing Durham needs flexible funding alongside existing local law enforcement partnerships.

agenda_items.title: Educator Vacancies, Compensation, and Retiree Rehire Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members and Superintendent Pascal Mubenga discussed critical vacancies—especially in Exceptional Children (EC) and bus drivers—urging state relief on six-month retiree rehire restrictions, restoration of master's degree pay, and inclusion of urban counties like Durham and Wake in state teacher salary supplement funds. Senator Natalie Murdock and Representative Zach Hawkins noted bipartisan rural/urban impacts and discussed teacher diversity and IDD caucus efforts.

agenda_items.title: Mental Health, Universal School Meals, Capital Needs, and General Assembly Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Delegation members and board representatives discussed universal school meals, the insufficiency of a proposed $5 million statewide mental health allocation, school nursing partnerships, and DPS's aging facilities (averaging 45 years old) alongside potential state school capital bonds. Representative Marcia Morey warned of renewed parental rights legislation affecting K-3 instruction and advocated juvenile justice reforms requiring administrator sign-off on SRO court petitions, while Senator Mike Woodard requested DPS vacancy fact sheets for budget negotiations.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 12/8/22
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its December monthly work session, hearing a superintendent update on the Growing Together initiative as RTI International compiled community engagement data ahead of the January application window and a potential December 19 special meeting. During public comment, LGBTQ+ advocates and parents urged passage of comprehensive gender-support policies and training, while community speakers called for a multi-decade renewable energy and climate action plan leveraging federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and Inflation Reduction Act funding. Board members also reviewed equity training, restorative practices, disaggregated suspension data—highlighting a need for specific strategic plan targets to reduce suspensions among students with disabilities—and RTI's strategic plan feedback themes. Following a closed session covering litigation (KI v. DPS and KBB v. DPS) and personnel, the board unanimously approved the December 8 personnel report and a 2022-23 contract with the PACES program.

meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners held their quarterly joint meeting the morning after certification of the $400 million 2022 education bond referendum. Officials discussed applying the $400M bond and Limited Obligation Bonds toward the ~$944M–$996M plan, transitioning kitchens (e.g., Mangum) from gas to electric appliances, tracking bond-funded projects publicly, and coordinating future uses for vacated school land.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/17/22
disagreements.issue: Procedural Process vs. Immediate First-Reading Adoption of Draft LGBTQ+ Gender Support Policy
disagreements.summary: Board members debated whether to vote immediately on a member-drafted LGBTQ+ policy on first reading or follow formal agenda-notice procedures by directing staff and legal counsel to bring a vetted Orange County-model policy to the next meeting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance a foundational policy immediately rather than waiting for task force completion or further delay.
side_a_arguments: Community families have advocated for months and expect visible leadership to put a baseline policy in the policy manual.
Policies adapted from Orange and Buncombe counties are already vetted and reviewed by members and can be revised later as a living document.
Passing a formal directive ensures accountability rather than relying on informal expectations.
disagreements.side_b_position: Follow formal governance notice procedures and clarify whether administration is revising existing Gender Support Guidelines or drafting a new policy before voting.
side_b_arguments: The item was added to the agenda solely for discussion, not as a posted action item or first reading for public notice.
Passing policy without a finalized document posted on the agenda ahead of time departs from the board's governance and policy-committee process.
Board Attorney Rod Malone recommended directing staff and counsel to bring a reviewed draft to the next meeting, when the board could waive second reading if satisfied.
disagreements.resolution: The board reached consensus and voted 7-0 on Alexandra Valladares's motion (seconded by Natalie Beyer) directing administration to bring an LGBTQ+ gender support policy based on the Orange County model to the next board meeting, paired with a time-limited task force.

disagreements.issue: City of Durham Request to Mount ShotSpotter Acoustic Sensors on DPS School Buildings
disagreements.summary: Board members debated a City of Durham request for an MOA allowing ShotSpotter gunshot detection devices to be mounted on school parapet walls, weighing intergovernmental deference and potential response-time benefits against student surveillance concerns.
disagreements.side_a_position: Decline mounting ShotSpotter surveillance devices on school buildings and focus city-school partnerships on root causes of gun violence.
side_a_arguments: Placing acoustic surveillance equipment on school buildings sends an undesirable message to students and represents excessive surveillance.
Other mounting locations exist for the city's already-approved project, making school buildings unnecessary.
Collaboration with the city should prioritize addressing the root causes of gun violence, and some expressed interest in a buffer zone around schools.
disagreements.side_b_position: Respect the City Council's approved ShotSpotter pilot and consider potential emergency response-time benefits.
side_b_arguments: Durham City Council already voted to approve ShotSpotter, and inter-body collaboration favors deferring to the city's judgment on its program.
Acoustic detection could provide single-digit-second improvements in emergency response time if shots are fired near a school.
disagreements.resolution: Board Attorney Rod Malone advised that a motion was only needed to move forward with an MOA, not to decline it. No board member made a motion to proceed, so the administration took no action to place ShotSpotter devices on DPS schools.

meetings.title: Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 8/11/22 | 5:30
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Chair Jovonia Lewis with Matt Sears participating virtually, the August 11, 2022 work session covered back-to-school readiness, school safety governance, purchasing policy revisions, and science education partnerships. The board amended its agenda to add COVID-19 and after-school updates, approved the June 9 minutes and an amended consent agenda (expanding the Edmentum/Study Island contract to all DPS schools), and voted 7-0 to appoint Alejandra Gomez to the educator vacancy on the Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force ahead of anticipated SRO MOU feedback. Administration presented back-to-school staffing, after-school waitlists, and COVID-19 protocols alongside first readings of purchasing and construction policy amendments raising staff contract and change-order thresholds ($300,000 for services; $500,000 for construction bidding and change orders). The board also unanimously renewed the Museum of Life and Science contract and, after a closed session from which Matt Sears departed, approved the amended August 11 personnel report 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 7B: Back-to-School After-School Staffing and COVID-19 Protocols
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported receiving 20 after-school job applications (with one hire assigned to Lyons Farm Elementary) and clarified how sibling waitlists operate. meetings.title: Board of Education Summer Retreat | August 3, 2022
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead convened the morning session of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education summer retreat, with Vice Chair Matt Sears participating virtually and staff resolving initial audio echo issues. Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy and district staff presented strategic plan progress across key priorities, highlighting the Evening Academy's earlier October start in 2021-22, expansion of restorative practice centers, and community-building student groups including We Are Kings, We Are Queens, and LGBTQ+ groups. Priority 4 staff outlined school, family, and community engagement gains, including increased storytelling, a partnership effectiveness rubric, and potential launch of a district mobile app. In the Human Resources presentation, Dr. Lusane and team addressed statewide licensure and recruitment challenges, reported progress toward Goal 3B (7% Latino staff toward a 10% target by 2023), discussed TA-to-Teacher, Durham Tech, and bus driver CDL pipelines, and confirmed an external salary study scheduled for completion in December 2022; no formal votes were taken before the lunch recess.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Strategic Plan Retreat Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the Board of Education summer retreat following initial audio echo troubleshooting and recognized Vice Chair Matt Sears attending virtually. District leaders introduced the strategic plan organized around five priorities and previewed small-group board activities to review multi-year implementation progress.

agenda_items.title: Academic and Student Support Progress: Evening Academy, Student Groups, and Restorative Practices
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following small-group breakout sessions, Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy and staff reviewed strategic plan progress on student support initiatives. Staff highlighted starting the Evening Academy earlier in October during 2021-22 with core subject teachers and a social worker, expanding student affinity groups (including We Are Kings, We Are Queens, and LGBTQ+ groups) with the Office of Equity Affairs, and embedding restorative practice centers in schools to address code-of-conduct infractions.

agenda_items.title: Priority 4 Update: School, Family, and Community Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented an overview of Priority 4 family and community engagement initiatives, citing expanded district storytelling and Dr. Denner's programming. Presenters also highlighted a partnership effectiveness rubric for schools to evaluate external partnerships and discussed interest in developing a district mobile application alongside community members.

agenda_items.title: Human Resources Update: Recruitment, Retention, Latino Staff Goal 3B, and Salary Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Lusane presented HR recruitment and retention data, noting increased reliance on residency and emergency teaching licenses and calling for state-level recruitment action rather than inter-district recycling. Staff reported 7% Latino staff toward Goal 3B's 10% target by 2023, expanded Spanish-speaking HR staff, school HR report cards, TA-to-Teacher and Durham Tech graduate pipelines (~1,800 DPS seniors annually), CDL bus driver pathways, substitute pool needs, and an external salary study (job descriptions under review) scheduled to conclude in December 2022. Chair Umstead recessed the retreat for lunch at 03:49:50.

meetings.title: Board of Education Retreat
meetings.executive_summary: Reconvening after lunch for the afternoon retreat session, Chair Bettina Umstead and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga led a comprehensive review of the Growing Together initiative, featuring newly presented financial projections for the recently approved elementary boundaries and regional application programs. Staff estimated net additional annual costs ranging from cost-neutral up to $1.5 million depending on operational savings, covering programs such as IB at E.K. Powe, dual language immersion expansion, a $55,000 dual language coordinator, and district-wide elementary global language exposure. Board members Natalie Beyer and Matt Sears questioned global language outcomes and strongly criticized remote or virtual language instruction for young children, while staff outlined community outreach strategies and poverty/equity datasets including SNAP and McKinney-Vento metrics. The board then participated in an informal dot-voting continuum workshop on future secondary school Growing Together priorities, followed by Dr. Mubenga's back-to-school staffing vacancy update before adjournment.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together Review and Financial Projections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead reconvened the retreat and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and staff presented the financial component for the Growing Together elementary plan adopted in July. Presenters reviewed the 30-year context since the 1992 district merger, Policy 4150, upcoming schools Lyons Farm and Murray-Massenberg, and recurring operational, personnel, and startup costs (including IB staffing at E.K. Powe, a $55,000 dual language coordinator, and global language), projecting net new costs between $0 and $1.5 million depending on projected savings.

agenda_items.title: Board Discussion on Global Language Outcomes, Coordinator Pay, and Virtual Instruction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members questioned staff regarding expected language proficiency outcomes for elementary global language instruction, funding for instructional supplies, and standardizing coordinator salaries across DPS. Natalie Beyer and Vice Chair Matt Sears both expressed strong reservations about virtual or remote instruction for young elementary students, urging in-person funding support with county commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Community Engagement Strategy and Equity Datasets
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff including Matthew Palmer discussed expanding outreach beyond conventional robocalls to reach both current DPS families and parents of preschool-aged children. Presenters reviewed the use of equity datasets—including SNAP and McKinney-Vento homelessness metrics—while addressing the legacy of redlining and community desire for strong neighborhood schools.

agenda_items.title: Secondary Program Continuum Workshop (Dot-Voting Exercise)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff facilitated an interactive blue, green, and red dot-voting and sticky-note workshop across six pairs of priorities to gather board input for future secondary Growing Together planning. Board members debriefed tradeoffs around extending specialized programs like dual language immersion into high school, audition/portfolio admissions versus random lotteries or sibling priorities, geographic distribution, and aligning offerings with career and workforce realities.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent Back-to-School Vacancy Update and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mubenga updated the board on staffing ahead of traditional school opening, reporting that year-round schools were operating smoothly with only one or two vacancies and committing to send families a detailed vacancy and coverage plan one week before traditional schools open. Chair Umstead noted a board team-building session would be rescheduled when all members were free from open-house conflicts and adjourned the retreat at 02:01:11.

meetings.title: Board of Education Organizational Meeting | July 8, 2022 | 8:30AM
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 8, 2022 organizational meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education received certified May 2022 election results from the Durham County Board of Elections (24.38% turnout among 232,510 eligible voters) and swore in reelected and newly elected members Emily Chávez, Bettina Umstead, Matt Sears (virtually), Natalie Beyer, and Millicent Rogers. Under Policy 2200, the board unanimously reelected Bettina Umstead as Chair (7-0) and elected Matt Sears as Vice Chair (7-0) via roll call votes. Members also unanimously approved the 2022-2023 board meeting schedule (7-0) after agreeing on 5:30 p.m. work sessions and 6:30 p.m. regular meetings to balance member commutes and timely adjournment. Following unanimous approval of campus maintenance consent contracts (7-0), an agenda amendment for an open-session personnel item (7-0), and a closed session (7-0), the board returned to open session and unanimously approved the July 8, 2022 personnel report (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Certificates of Election, and Oaths of Office
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the organizational meeting to order and led a moment of silence, with Matt Sears and Jovonia Lewis joining virtually. Durham County Board of Elections Director Bowens presented certified May 2022 election results (56,696 ballots cast, 24.38% turnout) and certificates of election to Emily Chávez (District 1), Bettina Umstead (District 2), Matt Sears (District 3), Natalie Beyer (District 4), and Millicent Rogers (Consolidated District B, filling the remainder of the term expiring 2024), after which oaths of office were administered.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair and Vice Chair (Policy 2200)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga presided over the Chair election under Policy 2200; Alexandra Valladares nominated Bettina Umstead, who was reelected 7-0 by roll call. Resuming the gavel, Chair Umstead opened Vice Chair nominations, and Matt Sears was unanimously elected Vice Chair 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2022-2023 Board of Education Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Alexandra Valladares moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the 2022-2023 board meeting schedule. Beyer inquired about setting a 5:30 p.m. start time for work sessions (alongside 6:30 p.m. regular meetings) to accommodate Valladares's commute while ensuring staff could wrap up before Friday, which Sears and Lewis supported before a 7-0 roll call vote.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Campus Maintenance Contracts) and Agenda Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the consent agenda covering campus maintenance contracts to prepare schools for student return (7-0). Members then voted 7-0 to amend the agenda to add an open-session personnel action item following closed session.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Approval of July 8, 2022 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 7-0 on roll call to enter closed session at 00:32:02. Returning to open session at 01:19:29, Dr. Mubenga requested approval of the July 8, 2022 personnel report, which the board approved unanimously 7-0 by roll call before adjourning at 01:20:18.
